_note: Working applicability hypotheses for the five CYBER-BRIDGE pilots (energy, software, public administration, law enforcement, IoT). Partner names are left for each pilot owner to enter; roles are hypotheses to confirm with the pilot and with ENC. DRAFT-VERIFY.

profiles.name: Energy pilot
profiles.basis: NIS2 Annex I, sector 1 (energy). Essential entity if above the size thresholds or designated.
focus: NIS2 Art. 23 reporting clocks on a live incident
Art. 21(2)(d) supply chain for OT and field devices

profiles.name: Software pilot
profiles.basis: CRA manufacturer of products with digital elements. NIS2 role to confirm (only if the company is itself in Annex I/II scope).
focus: CRA Art. 14 reporting, in force since 11.09.2026
SBOM and CSAF advisories ingested as evidence
Annex I Part II vulnerability handling
profiles.assets: Software products, update service, build pipeline

profiles.name: Public administration pilot
profiles.basis: NIS2 Annex I, sector 10 (public administration of central government), as transposed nationally.
focus: Art. 21(2)(i) access control and asset management

profiles.name: Law enforcement pilot
profiles.basis: NIS2 Art. 2(7) excludes public administration entities acting in law enforcement. No mandatory obligation engages; the pilot tracks NIS2 Art. 21 in voluntary alignment.
focus: Applicability engine returns nothing mandatory, and says why
Evidence handling and cross-border incident information

profiles.name: IoT pilot
profiles.basis: CRA manufacturer. Important entity if in NIS2 Annex II, sector 5 (manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products).
focus: CRA Annex I Part I: secure by default, updates, attack surface
SBOM per product, not per organisation
Both regimes engaged on one incident

profiles.name: EnergyGate Distributie SA
profiles.basis: Worked example from the original T3.1 demonstrator. Fictional; not a CYBER-BRIDGE pilot partner.
focus: Both regimes engaged by one organisation
profiles.assets: RTU-400 remote terminal unit, Update Service
